subject: Lewis Jones, Co. B U.S. Colored Infantry
source: NPS Civil War Soldiers and Sailors System (CWSS)
query: exact phrase "Jones, Lewis" + filter State = United States Colored Troops
note: Fuzzy search returns 7706; exact phrase gives 48. Units include 2nd, 3rd, 13th, 23rd, 24th, 25th, 28th, 29th, 47th, 48th, 58th, 67th, 96th, 100th USCI, 4th/5th/6th USC Cavalry, 9th USC Heavy Artillery, and one Unassigned.

subject: Lewis Jones - 23rd USCI candidate
note: STRONGEST CANDIDATE: the 23rd USCI was organised in Virginia (Camp Casey, Arlington) and recruited Northern Virginia, incl. Loudoun. BUT the CWSS COMPANY field is BLANK, so it cannot confirm "Co. B". Film M589 roll 49; plaque number B-39; CWSS note: "See also 28 U.S.C.T."

subject: Lewis Jones service record
source: FamilySearch, Compiled Military Service Records ... U.S. Colored Troops 1861-1866
note: 933,027 records / 759,894 images, free. Index carries Military Unit but NOT company. Covers only a portion of units (1st-5th USC Cavalry, infantry organisations 36th-40th), so the 23rd is not in this collection.

subject: Lewis Jones service record
source: FamilySearch, Civil War Service Records of Union Colored Troops 1863-1865
note: Broader collection. Sample record (ark JWYX-Q94) shows the field set: Name, Age, Birth Year (Estimated), Military Unit, Event Date, Affiliate Publication Number. NO COMPANY FIELD and Event Place is only "United States", so neither company nor enlistment place can be filtered.

subject: Delila J. Jones widow's pension
source: FamilySearch, General Index to Pension Files 1861-1934 (NARA T288)
note: Delila Jones widow of Samuel W Jones (Indiana Twp, Lincoln, Kansas, 1888); Delila Jones widow of Eli A Jones (1883); Delila A Jones widow of George W Jones (Tennessee, Drew, Arkansas, 1881).

subject: Delila J. Jones widow's pension
source: FamilySearch, Civil War and Later Pension Index 1861-1917
note: No federal widow's pension traceable for her under this name. Meaningful rather than merely negative: many USCT widows could not document a marriage performed in slavery and so never qualified.

source: Library of Virginia, Virginia Untold (Primo, vid=01LVA_INST:VU)
result: 17 registers survive; Loudoun NOT among them
note: LEAD CLOSED. The surviving Virginia cohabitation registers are Goochland, Henry, Clarke, Culpeper, Fluvanna, Westmoreland, Scott, Washington, Montgomery, Smyth, Wythe, Caroline, Augusta, Roanoke, Lunenburg, Prince Edward and Floyd. subject: Delila Jones in unindexed records
query: q.text="Delila Jones" with Place filter = Virginia (applied via the on-screen checkbox tree; URL params alone do not drive it)
result: 46 Virginia hits, 15 after filtering; NONE in Loudoun or Northern Virginia
note: Counties hit were Wythe, Pittsylvania, Southampton, Brunswick and Bath. A meaningful negative - see the control search in the next row.

subject: Is Loudoun in the full-text corpus?
note: CONTROL SEARCH confirming the corpus covers Loudoun: Marriage Records 1751-1880, Will Books (2-E 1850, 2-P 1860-65, 2-Q 1865-66), Deed Books (5-O 1856-57, 5-R 1859, 6-I 1876-77) and more. So Delila's absence from Loudoun full text is evidence, not a gap in coverage.

subject: Possible Delila in an 1850 Loudoun will
note: SPECULATIVE BUT WORTH READING. ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G9P6-S35N, film 007645058, Loudoun Will Books 1757-1879. Delila J. Jones would have been 12-17 in 1850, and enslaved people are named in wills, so an enslaved girl called Delila in an 1850 Loudoun will is a plausible lead. Reading the matched line needs the transcript panel on the image viewer; the name alone cannot confirm it.

subject: Loudoun gravestone transcriptions 1948-1950
query: surfaced incidentally by the Tavenner control search
result: IN THE CORPUS and full-text searchable
note: BEST FIND OF THIS ROUND, for the project rather than for Lewis Jones. 'Inscriptions from Cemeteries' and 'Cemetery Records', Loudoun, Virginia, Gravestone Transcription Records 1948-1950 - almost certainly the DAR-era survey this README lists as a next source. It predates seventy-five years of weathering, so it should resolve date conflicts and may recover inscriptions since lost, including stones at Pleasant Valley.

subject: Order the compiled service record
note: Ordering needs a form submission and a payment, so it has to be placed by hand. Use the CWSS citation: Lewis Jones, Private, 23rd Regiment USCI, film M589 roll 49, plaque B-39, note 'See also 28 U.S.C.T.' Order via NATF Form 86 or NARA's online system. Ancestry Library Edition at Balch likewise needs a library card or an in-person visit.
